## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `docs/agents/sm_github.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: docs-freshness CI fails — generated agent doc is stale**

This PR edits the human doc `docs/agents/sm_github.md`, but the generated copy `docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md` was not regenerated and committed. The `docs-freshness` check (`.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml`) runs `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails on any `git diff` under `docs/agents/generated` — it is red on this PR.

I reproduced it locally on the PR branch:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git diff --stat -- docs/agents/generated
# docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md | 9 +++++++++
```

The diff is exactly the new "Merge-window cadence (gh-837)" section this PR added to the human doc — the generator embeds the human doc, so any edit to `docs/agents/sm_github.md` requires a regeneration commit.

**Fix**:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md
git commit -m "gh-837 regenerate agent docs"
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: per-tick 📊 cost line fires even with the knob at default 1**

`reportValidationCost` is called unconditionally after the rule loop, so every SM tick — including every deployment that never sets `validationConcurrency` (the knob ships at 1, i.e. all of production today) — now prints a `📊 gh-837 validation cost — merge-window slots 0/1 in use …` line. That is permanent new noise in the tick log for a report that only matters when the parallel window is active.

Consider gating the log on something like `mutexMax > 1 || slotsInUse > 0` (keeping the `validationCost` field on the action result unconditional if downstream wants it). The tick already stays quiet about the knob when `cfg.max === 1` in the arming patch above, so this would match that philosophy.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: label-filtering logic is triplicated**

The same `labels.map(...)` + draft/blocked/`pr_approved` filter shape appears three times: `slotsInUse` here, `depth` just below, and again in `approvedQueueDepth` (~line 3530). Consider extracting one helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function approvedPrs(list) {
    return list.filter(function (p) {
        if (!p || p.draft) return false;
        var labels = (p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
        return labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1 && labels.indexOf('pr_approved') !== -1;
    });
}
```

Then `slotsInUse = approvedPrs(list).filter(holds ai_validating).length` and `depth = approvedPrs(list).length` — keeping the three call sites from drifting apart on the `blocked`/draft semantics.

---

### Thread 4

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

```javascript

    return list.filter(function (p) {
        if (!p || p.draft) return false;

    });

```

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38046867202) · started 11:00 · done 11:09 ✅

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: docs-freshness CI fails — generated agent doc is stale**

This PR edits the human doc `docs/agents/sm_github.md`, but the generated copy `docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md` was not regenerated and committed. The `docs-freshness` check (`.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml`) runs `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails on any `git diff` under `docs/agents/generated` — it is red on this PR.

I reproduced it locally on the PR branch:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git diff --stat -- docs/agents/generated
# docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md | 9 +++++++++
```

The diff is exactly the new "Merge-window cadence (gh-837)" section this PR added to the human doc — the generator embeds the human doc, so any edit to `docs/agents/sm_github.md` requires a regeneration commit.

**Fix**:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md
git commit -m "gh-837 regenerate agent docs"
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: per-tick 📊 cost line fires even with the knob at default 1**

`reportValidationCost` is called unconditionally after the rule loop, so every SM tick — including every deployment that never sets `validationConcurrency` (the knob ships at 1, i.e. all of production today) — now prints a `📊 gh-837 validation cost — merge-window slots 0/1 in use …` line. That is permanent new noise in the tick log for a report that only matters when the parallel window is active.

Consider gating the log on something like `mutexMax > 1 || slotsInUse > 0` (keeping the `validationCost` field on the action result unconditional if downstream wants it). The tick already stays quiet about the knob when `cfg.max === 1` in the arming patch above, so this would match that philosophy.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: label-filtering logic is triplicated**

The same `labels.map(...)` + draft/blocked/`pr_approved` filter shape appears three times: `slotsInUse` here, `depth` just below, and again in `approvedQueueDepth` (~line 3530). Consider extracting one helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function approvedPrs(list) {
    return list.filter(function (p) {
        if (!p || p.draft) return false;
        var labels = (p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
        return labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1 && labels.indexOf('pr_approved') !== -1;
    });
}
```

Then `slotsInUse = approvedPrs(list).filter(holds ai_validating).length` and `depth = approvedPrs(list).length` — keeping the three call sites from drifting apart on the `blocked`/draft semantics.

---

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `docs/agents/sm_github.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: docs-freshness CI fails — generated agent doc is stale**

This PR edits the human doc `docs/agents/sm_github.md`, but the generated copy `docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md` was not regenerated and committed. The `docs-freshness` check (`.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml`) runs `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails on any `git diff` under `docs/agents/generated` — it is red on this PR.

I reproduced it locally on the PR branch:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git diff --stat -- docs/agents/generated
# docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md | 9 +++++++++
```

The diff is exactly the new "Merge-window cadence (gh-837)" section this PR added to the human doc — the generator embeds the human doc, so any edit to `docs/agents/sm_github.md` requires a regeneration commit.

**Fix**:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md
git commit -m "gh-837 regenerate agent docs"
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: per-tick 📊 cost line fires even with the knob at default 1**

`reportValidationCost` is called unconditionally after the rule loop, so every SM tick — including every deployment that never sets `validationConcurrency` (the knob ships at 1, i.e. all of production today) — now prints a `📊 gh-837 validation cost — merge-window slots 0/1 in use …` line. That is permanent new noise in the tick log for a report that only matters when the parallel window is active.

Consider gating the log on something like `mutexMax > 1 || slotsInUse > 0` (keeping the `validationCost` field on the action result unconditional if downstream wants it). The tick already stays quiet about the knob when `cfg.max === 1` in the arming patch above, so this would match that philosophy.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: label-filtering logic is triplicated**

The same `labels.map(...)` + draft/blocked/`pr_approved` filter shape appears three times: `slotsInUse` here, `depth` just below, and again in `approvedQueueDepth` (~line 3530). Consider extracting one helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function approvedPrs(list) {
    return list.filter(function (p) {
        if (!p || p.draft) return false;
        var labels = (p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
        return labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1 && labels.indexOf('pr_approved') !== -1;
    });
}
```

Then `slotsInUse = approvedPrs(list).filter(holds ai_validating).length` and `depth = approvedPrs(list).length` — keeping the three call sites from drifting apart on the `blocked`/draft semantics.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #838._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `docs/agents/sm_github.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: docs-freshness CI fails — generated agent doc is stale**

This PR edits the human doc `docs/agents/sm_github.md`, but the generated copy `docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md` was not regenerated and committed. The `docs-freshness` check (`.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml`) runs `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails on any `git diff` under `docs/agents/generated` — it is red on this PR.

I reproduced it locally on the PR branch:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git diff --stat -- docs/agents/generated
# docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md | 9 +++++++++
```

The diff is exactly the new "Merge-window cadence (gh-837)" section this PR added to the human doc — the generator embeds the human doc, so any edit to `docs/agents/sm_github.md` requires a regeneration commit.

**Fix**:

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated/sm_github.md
git commit -m "gh-837 regenerate agent docs"
```

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: per-tick 📊 cost line fires even with the knob at default 1**

`reportValidationCost` is called unconditionally after the rule loop, so every SM tick — including every deployment that never sets `validationConcurrency` (the knob ships at 1, i.e. all of production today) — now prints a `📊 gh-837 validation cost — merge-window slots 0/1 in use …` line. That is permanent new noise in the tick log for a report that only matters when the parallel window is active.

Consider gating the log on something like `mutexMax > 1 || slotsInUse > 0` (keeping the `validationCost` field on the action result unconditional if downstream wants it). The tick already stays quiet about the knob when `cfg.max === 1` in the arming patch above, so this would match that philosophy.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: label-filtering logic is triplicated**

The same `labels.map(...)` + draft/blocked/`pr_approved` filter shape appears three times: `slotsInUse` here, `depth` just below, and again in `approvedQueueDepth` (~line 3530). Consider extracting one helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function approvedPrs(list) {
    return list.filter(function (p) {
        if (!p || p.draft) return false;
        var labels = (p.labels || []).map(function (l) { return (l && l.name) || l; });
        return labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1 && labels.indexOf('pr_approved') !== -1;
    });
}
```

Then `slotsInUse = approvedPrs(list).filter(holds ai_validating).length` and `depth = approvedPrs(list).length` — keeping the three call sites from drifting apart on the `blocked`/draft semantics.

- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).

- **PR #**: 838
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/838
- **Title**: gh-837 [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min parallel validation or merge-train needed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-837` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +869
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T11:00:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T11:20:45Z

## PR Description

Closes #837
### What changed
Implemented the gh-837 parallel-validations option for the SM merge window: `jobParams.validationConcurrency` (default 1 = unchanged serial behavior; `.dmtools/config.js` `smValidationConcurrency` overrides, clamped to 5) relaxes the `ai_validating`/`pr_approved` mutex to N concurrent arms once the approved queue depth reaches `validationConcurrencyQueueWatermark` (default 3). The SM patches `query.mutexMax` onto validate-armed + the revalidate twins and raises the arm limit to the cap so every free slot fills in one tick; githubSource and the validate_pr action-time re-check both defer only at the cap.

### Key decisions
- **Arm simultaneity is the cadence lever**: the L2 replay showed a limit-1 arm staggers parallel validations by a tick, so the second concludes after the first merge and its run is wasted on the moved base — simultaneous arms let the mergeBot's one-run batch land both merges in one window.
- **Runner cost hard-capped** (AC2): at most N validations in flight; per-tick validation-minutes report on the tick log + action result (`validationCost`).
- **Red handling untouched** (AC3): fail-validation stays per-PR — a red parks exactly one head, no cross-contamination; dev lane (`mutexAmong [pr_approved]`) unaffected.
- **Replay numbers** (`test_mergeCadence.js`, queue depth 6, validation 35 min): serial ~50 min/merge → parallel-2 ~25 min/merge (AC1 ≤30 target met; owner 1/h floor holds).
- AC4 (live 4h soak) is L3 and cannot run in dev — knob ships at default 1, so production behavior is bit-identical until the var is flipped.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 2411 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-837: [GOAL] SM factory merge cadence: owner expects 1 merge / 30 min (floor 1/h) — serial refresh+validate cycle caps at ~1/45-60 min; parallel validation or merge-train needed

## Description

## Goal

Steady-state merge cadence into the SM factory main of ~1 merge per 30 minutes (owner expectation 2026-10-10; acceptable floor 1/hour). Current design ceiling is ~1 merge / 45-60 min.

## Subject

The SM merge window's strictly serial cycle. Per merge, every approved head pays:
1. BEHIND-refresh after the previous merge moves main (silent-update, ~1 head per tick, ticks ~5 min apart → ~10-15 min);
2. a fresh full validation CI on the refreshed head (~30-40 min: Quality gate + platform legs);
3. the merge itself.
Single-flight `ai_validating` mutex (runner-budget protection) forbids overlapping validations. Live numbers 2026-10-10: 4 merges by 10:30Z (two 4h gaps were the header_badge_pty flake deadlock + the red-verdict loop #832, not the cadence); healthy interval #1470→#1453 = 50 min. Approved queue depth hit 10 during the stall — drain at 1/h takes longer than the queue builds.

## Capability surface (options — analyze, pick, implement)

- **Parallel validations (N=2-3)**: relax mutexAmong [pr_approved] to allow N concurrent validations; runner-cost bounded via a concurrency knob (repo var), default 1 (today's behavior) — flip to 2/3 when the approved queue exceeds a watermark.
- **Merge-train**: merge K approved heads in one window after validating the BATCH result (validate head K against main+1..K-1 stacked) — GitHub-native merge-queue style; highest throughput, needs strict green-gate on the stacked tree.
- **Validation wall-time cut**: shard/skip platform legs for queue-drain mode (publish isn't gated on platform legs per #1368 — the aggregate still is; audit what the merge window actually needs).
- Priority-aware ordering if `priority_blocker` labels should jump the FIFO queue (currently ignored).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/replay — with queue depth ≥4, sustained cadence ≤30 min/merge (or documented floor with the chosen option).
2. AC2: runner cost reported per tick (tokens analog: validation-minutes) — no unbounded growth.
3. AC3: a red validation in parallel mode parks exactly one head (#832 semantics preserved); no cross-contamination.
4. AC4: live — a 4-hour observation window with queue depth ≥3 shows p50 interval ≤30 min and zero deadlock-class stalls.

## Test plan

- L1: rule-level unit tests (mutex relaxation, batch validation verdict mapping, priority ordering).
- L2: replay 2026-10-10 (deadlock + drain) under the new option — no stall recurs, drain time measured.
- L3 (live): 4h soak with the knob at 2; watch runner saturation and red-handling.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT validates (quality gates stay).
- The #832 red-loop fix (independent, already reviewed).

## References

- Owner expectation: 2026-10-10 "раз в 30 мин примерно... или хотя бы раз в 1 час".
- Live cycle evidence: fa-state histories (pr-1453 12-cycle), #1474 validation dispatched 10:24:49Z in_progress at 10:3x.
- Single-flight mutex origin: gh-748/921/922 family (runner budget).
